primary_claim: Across a suite of 8 sparse autoencoders trained on different layers of a CLIP Vision Transformer, layer 20 is the most monosemantic layer (by the Sort Eval Autointerpretability technique) and has the most frequently activating features, making it a reasonable alternative to the more commonly used layer 22.

effect.metric: Sort Eval Autointerpretability monosemanticity / feature activation frequency
effect.value: layer 20 ranked most monosemantic and most frequently activating among 8 trained layers

contradicts_or_qualifies: suggests layer 20, rather than the more commonly used layer 22 from prior visual SAE work, is a reasonable (or better) layer choice
limitations_stated: have not demonstrated anything to a high degree of rigor
quote: Using the Sort Eval Autointerpretability technique introduced by Anthropic we found that layer 20 seems to be the most monosemantic layer.
